value.body: Works at an oil or gas drilling site, examining rock cuttings and gas readings carried up in the drilling fluid to record which rock layers are being drilled. Oilfield service companies hire mud loggers for onshore and offshore rigs. Work is in a logging unit on the rig, in shifts, for set periods on site followed by time off.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Sc / M.Sc Geology, or B.Tech Petroleum Engineering

items.label: Work pattern
items.value: Rotational — weeks on site, then weeks off

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Microscopes, gas detectors, sensors and logging software

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers are hired as trainee mud loggers by oilfield service companies, usually after a geology degree. Selection checks geology basics and fitness for remote and offshore work; offshore postings need safety and survival training, typically arranged by the employer.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Describing rock cuttings under a microscope
Reading gas and drilling sensor data

value.title: At a glance
items: Remote rig life, shift work and long rotations are part of the job.
Experience can lead to wellsite geologist or data engineer roles.
Hiring follows oil and gas drilling activity, so it can rise and fall.
